explanation: Afonso de Albuquerque took it as a base for Portugal's Indian Ocean trade. Indian troops took Goa in 1961, ending 451 years of Portuguese rule.

claims.text: Portuguese forces under Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510.
Portugal held Goa until 1961, more than 450 years.
Calicut was never a Portuguese colony, Bombay was Portuguese only from 1534 to 1661, and Madras was a British settlement.
India took control of Goa by military action in December 1961.
